messages:
maria chen: Heads-up — running into noisy billing/telemetry for API keys that don't include a project claim. This is blowing out the per-project dashboards. Thinking we need a short sampling + attribution fallback before we flip the new quota mapping. anyone available for a quick sync? /cc @aj patel
aj patel: on it. do we have concrete examples of requests missing project vs requests with wrong org claim? could be client-side libs or old SDKs.
oliver park: i pulled a sample — ~0.6% of requests in last 24h have `project_id` null but include `org_id`. they're currently being attributed to the org default project which messes up per-project quotas.
henry nguyen: we should avoid changing billing semantics silently. propose: (a) add telemetry tag `auth_fallback_reason` and `auth_attribution_path`, (b) sample 100% of unattributed requests for 30m after deploy, (c) show sampled examples in console. if rate > 0.1% after 10m rollback.
maria chen: agreed. my worry: support and customers will see sudden quota hits. timeline idea: keep old mapping for 24h with visible console banner + per-route metrics, then flip if signal is green. who owns the rollout checklist?
aj patel: i'll drive the checklist. rough steps: 1) telemetry: emit `auth_fallback_reason` (enum: missing_claim, invalid_claim, inscrutable_token), 2) expose a sampled request table in console (sample id, headers, parsed claims), 3) add canary flag `auth.attribution_experiment` gated on org, 4) preflight job that runs mapping locally for a day to show deltas.
oliver park: for parsing clarity, here's a snippet of what we currently expect from the JWT claims — need to make sure fallback logic is explicit:
```
{
  "iss": "https://auth.redwood.ai",
  "sub": "service-account:sa-1234",
  "org_id": "org_42",
  "project_id": null,
  "scp": ["inference.generate"]
}
```
fallback logic proposal: prefer `project_id` if present, else if `sub` maps to a project via service-account registry use that, else attribute to `org_default_project` but mark telemetry `auth_fallback_reason=missing_claim`.
henry nguyen: dev-ops + billing want this in the playbook: exact alert thresholds, console banner text, and a safe revert button (manual + automated). also add a per-org dry-run metric that shows what billing attribution WOULD be if flipped.
maria chen: good call — the dry-run metric is critical. we can surface a delta estimate in the console (tokens affected, projected cost delta). keep it hidden by default, opt-in via canary flag.
aj patel: UX note for console: include a toggle in the org settings with a tooltip: "Preview attribution changes (dry-run) — shows projected quota and billing impacts for 24h". devex can sketch.
devex-bot: Canary job scheduled: infra/canary-auth-attrib-2024-11-02T10:00Z — will sample unattributed requests and ship `auth_fallback_reason` tag.
maria chen: next steps: aj to create PR for telemetry + canary flag, oliver to add local preflight diff job, henry to draft playbook (alerts + revert). aim to deploy canary tomorrow and keep 24h observation window before any global flip.
aj patel: on it — i'll post the PR link when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
henry nguyen: i'll draft the revert runbook and the exact alert query (promql) and drop it here for review.
maria chen: perfect. i'll update the console banner copy and coordinate comms with support. thanks everyone.
